sentences.1: The incoming nurse read the handover notes left by the night sister.
sentences.2: The notes said the sister planned to move the patient nearer the desk so that his breathing would be easier to monitor, since a bed near the desk let the night staff watch his chest rise without walking the ward.
sentences.3: The notes also recorded that his temperature had been normal at midnight.
sentences.4: They ended with a reminder to chart his medication at six.

readings_chosen: Sentence 1: 'left by the night sister' — open: a description of the notes / a happening of its own. Taken: the happening (line leaving, GIVEN); no second fact line, as it would carry the same content.
Sentence 1: 'read' and 'left' have no shape in the shape book. Taken: doer-verb-thing happenings, to be reported not checked.
Sentence 2: 'a bed near the desk' — open: the patient's bed / any bed near the desk. Taken: the patient's bed (line patientbed, filled in), since the clause goes on to 'his chest rise'.

Sentence 2: 'without walking the ward' — open: the watching needs no walking of the ward / the watching happens while the staff are not walking the ward. Taken: the first (line withoutwalk, filled in).

Sentence 2: 'so that his breathing would be easier to monitor' — open: the aim is ease of monitoring / the aim is that monitoring happens. Taken: 'the patient's breathing is monitored' (line plan), with 'would be easier' binned as degree and mood.
Sentence 2: 'since' — open: BECAUSE / SINCE. Taken: SINCE (line since1); the clause gives a reason for what the plan is expected to achieve, not a cause that has already produced anything.
Sentence 2: the step from 'watch his chest rise' to 'monitor his breathing' is not written. Taken: added as line chestlink (filled in, ALWAYS SHOWS); strength and kind are my choice.

Sentence 2: the move is of the patient alone while the reason speaks of a bed. Taken: read as the patient moving in his bed (line patientbed); the step from the move to the bed's position is left unwritten for the checker.
Sentence 3: 'at midnight' — open: a time to bin / a stage named in the fact. Taken: the stage (rule 13), so the fact cannot be confused with a fact about another time.
Sentence 4: 'They' — open: the notes / the reminders as a set. Taken: the notes.
Sentence 4: 'ended with a reminder' is the narrator's description of the document, so the fact is CLAIMED in the actual ledger and the reminder's command goes to the bin.
All things: the text speaks of no press, so every thing line records response to a press not stated rather than a guessed class.
